Terminology: agents, Assistants and Specialists
An agent is any model performing agentic work, including a model working from an ordinary chat. This describes its activity, not a separate product or a revival of the retired Agents system. Assistants and Specialists remain configured product types; either can act as an agent, but an agent need not be an Assistant or Specialist. Delegated workers are also agents when carrying out agentic work.
Use agent for the general execution role and Assistant/Specialist for the configured identity. Capitalisation in interface labels does not change that distinction. Refer explicitly to legacy Agents when discussing the former product, API or migration. This terminology does not restore the legacy Agents product, editor, catalogue or API beyond the existing migration arrangements.


Assistants and Specialists
Replace the legacy Agents API with the Assistants and Specialists APIs; retain legacy Agents API availability until April 2027. Preserve definitions, conversations, memory, references and run history, with compatibility checks, recoverable migration and explicit resolution of ambiguous conversions.
Specialists follow configured instructions for repeatable tasks, similar to custom GPTs/workspace agents. Retain relevant legacy Agents functionality and support a Specialist chat page on a Board. Specialists can run scheduled, recurring and event-triggered jobs through Automations and return authorised results/statuses; personal proactive check-ins and unsolicited conversations remain exclusive to Assistants. Rename the legacy Agents Space to Specialists Space.

requirements.requirement: Create, manage, nest, share and recover Spaces while preserving identity, policy inheritance and explicit capability bindings.

sources.quote:
The sidebar does not expose a ninth Custom type. Users create user-defined Spaces through + New Space and manage the hierarchy through Edit Spaces. User-created Spaces have SpaceOrigin = UserCreated and receive the full Space graph editor described below; built-in first-party Spaces have SpaceOrigin = BuiltIn and expose only the protected Events & Extensions editor.


Spaces MAY be nested through ParentSpaceID to create logical hierarchies. Nesting MUST preserve each Space’s stable identity and MUST NOT imply permission escalation. Child inheritance of sources, connected apps, model policy, memory, Skills, Plugins or Agents must be explicit/inspectable; a child cannot regain a capability or permission explicitly denied by a parent/security policy.


Edit Spaces MUST support reorder, nest/unnest, rename, icon, sharing, inheritance configuration, duplicate, archive/delete/recover and other structural management without exposing protected first-party internal implementation.

Space MUST contain at least SpaceID, SpaceOrigin, built-in type where applicable, Name, Icon?, ParentSpaceID?, owner/scope, instructions/configuration, model policy, context/source policy, memory policy, capability bindings, permissions, created/modified timestamps and revision metadata. SpaceID is stable across rename, nesting and UI ordering.

Every Space has its own capability bindings for Dulche Plugins, Skills and persistent Agents. By default, a newly created Space inherits all currently installed/enabled Dulche Plugins and Skills and all available Agents unless restricted by policy.


Space capability bindings MUST support inherited availability plus explicit per-Space enable/disable/exclusion and optional version pinning where the underlying package/Agent contract supports it. Installing a new globally enabled Plugin/Skill or making a new Agent available automatically makes it available to Spaces that still inherit that category.


Space bindings reference canonical Dulche package IDs/versions and Agent IDs; they MUST NOT clone package/Agent definitions into the Space. Availability does not grant permission: a Space may see a Plugin/Skill/Agent while still requiring the normal permission/trust decision before protected actions execute.

Spaces MAY be shared at Space or conversation level with explicit roles such as Viewer, Participant and Editor/Admin or equivalent typed scopes. Multi-human conversations MUST record AuthorPrincipalID per human message. Sharing a Space MUST NOT automatically share private external-account credentials or personal Den state.

sources.quote:
Spaces MUST use the Universal Model Picker. Effective model policy resolves explicit request override, conversation override, Space default, app/default policy and global default in that order, subject to capability/privacy/entitlement restrictions.


Switching model mid-conversation MUST NOT rewrite provenance of prior responses. Every AI response/run must retain effective model/provider identity and relevant policy provenance.

The Agentic Update defined in 9to1 Post-Release Updates is pulled forward into the current development push and is no longer gated on initial launch. The objective is to establish a production-capable agentic harness early enough that cloud models and eligible local models can execute the same durable work through the same typed app/tool interfaces, checkpoints, permissions, task state and recovery semantics. Cloud quota exhaustion, provider unavailability and equivalent model-routing failures MUST be recoverable routing conditions where an authorised eligible fallback exists. Switching models MUST resume the same canonical Task/Run rather than start a disconnected replacement chat, discard valid checkpoints or lose accepted work.

The framework-first phase MUST include a verified continuity path in which a durable task can survive model/provider interruption and continue on another authorised eligible route, including a local model when configured and capable, without creating a disconnected replacement task, losing accepted checkpoints or weakening permissions/privacy. This continuity requirement does not force cloud-to-local fallback when the user or policy has disabled it.

requirements.requirement: Attach typed sources with inspectable scope, current revisions, retrieval decisions and truthful citations.

sources.quote:
Spaces context MUST be represented as explicit typed references rather than opaque prompt stuffing. Supported reference families include Files/folders, Boards/pages, Write/Present/Canvas/Data artifacts, Mail threads/messages, Planner items, Map routes, Stack projects, Sites/projects, connected-app entities, conversations and uploaded sources.


Each context/source reference MUST retain stable source identity, revision/change token where applicable, permission state and ingestion/index state where required. Spaces must be able to detect that a referenced source has changed rather than treating an old snapshot as current.


A Sources/Context surface MUST let the user inspect what is attached, where it came from, current revision/availability, whether it is included automatically, ingestion/index status and remove/disable controls. Spaces MUST NOT rely on mysterious hidden context for ordinary operation.

Dragging/adding a folder SHOULD create a folder reference plus scope/filter configuration rather than eagerly duplicating every contained file. Spaces can retrieve authorised current files on demand through Files APIs.


Context budgeting and retrieval


When available material exceeds the selected model’s context, Dulche/Spaces MUST use deterministic context selection/retrieval. Required/current selection and explicit attached sources take priority over optional historical context. Retrieval/summarisation/omission decisions MUST be represented in run logs/Action Graph sufficiently for inspection.


Spaces MUST NOT claim that an answer considered an entire source set when only a subset was retrieved. Source-grounded modes must retain provenance for the chunks/entities actually used.

Web access MUST be an explicit Space/tool policy with at least Allowed, Ask and Disabled semantics where applicable. Source-only/closed-corpus workflows MUST be able to disable outside web retrieval completely.


When an answer materially relies on identifiable source material, Spaces MUST preserve clickable provenance/citations back to the underlying file/page/message/web source/entity where supported. It MUST distinguish source-derived claims from generated reasoning and must not claim support that the retrieved sources do not provide.

Change a source revision and submit a source-backed request against a source set larger than the selected context.

Closed-corpus requests cannot browse externally; changed, revoked, missing or ingestion-failed sources are explicit.

Retrieval/Action Graph traces and citation-to-passage checks.

requirements.requirement: Protect built-in graphs and validate full custom graphs with contextual AI and safe extension hooks.

sources.quote:
All Space graph editing uses the Home-owned Node Graph Framework also used by Automations. Home owns graph data structures, node registry, typed ports/connections, renderer, pan/zoom/selection, grouping, validation, clipboard/duplicate, undo/redo, graph versioning, execution visualisation hooks and contextual AI-bar integration. Spaces owns Space-specific event/action nodes and graph semantics; Dulche executes AI/model/Agent/tool portions; owning apps execute their typed actions.


Graph connections MUST be typed. Incompatible connections MUST be rejected or require an explicit conversion node. Graph nodes MUST reference stable canonical app/capability IDs rather than UI coordinates or screen controls.

Built-in Chat, Study, Tasks, Agent, Shopping, Research, Translate and Experiences Spaces expose a limited Events & Extensions graph editor attached only through published safe extension hooks. The protected first-party core graph/behaviour is not editable, disconnectable or replaceable.


Allowed extension hooks may include Space loaded/activated/deactivated/closed, conversation created/opened, response started/stopped/resumed/completed and relevant type-specific events such as Study session started/completed, Task started/blocked/completed, Research run completed, Translate Translation Set/job completed, Experience started/checkpointed/branched/completed or Agent run state changed.


Allowed extension actions may include Set Do Not Disturb, send Home notification, add/remove allowed context, open app/entity, create Planner item, invoke Automation/Agent/Skill/Plugin/permitted MCP capability, update extension-owned Space variables and add/show custom sidebar surfaces.


The built-in extension editor MUST NOT allow removal/replacement of protected sidebar items, suppression of required first-party events, replacement of the Space’s conversation/runtime behaviour, bypass of permissions, mutation of protected first-party graph internals, disabling required recovery/safety behaviour or creation of unbounded loops.


Published extension hooks are versioned. After a 9to1 update, incompatible/retired hooks MUST produce a needs-attention/repair state rather than silently breaking the whole Space.

User-created Spaces created through + New Space may use the full Space graph editor. Their graph may define lifecycle behaviour, conversation routing, source retrieval, model/Agent selection, logic/branching, state, app actions, Generative UI, custom sidebar surfaces and other authorised Space behaviour.


Full graphs MAY use bounded logic nodes such as If, Switch, Filter, Merge, Wait, bounded Loop, variables, compare/transform plus typed AI/runtime nodes such as Prompt model, Choose model, Run Agent, invoke Skill/Plugin/MCP, retrieve/search sources and Generate UI.


Full graphs MUST still obey Home permissions, Dulche runtime limits, package/Agent availability, target-app contracts and loop/budget safeguards. A graph is not a permission escalation mechanism.


Custom graph edits MUST use Draft versus Active revision semantics. Changes are validated before Apply/Publish; invalid drafts do not replace the last valid active graph. Prior active revisions SHOULD be rollback-capable.


Graph-editor AI bar


Both the built-in Events & Extensions editor and the full user-created Space graph editor MUST host the persistent contextual AI bar. The bar receives graph-semantic context and modifies graphs only through typed Node Graph APIs, never by mouse/keyboard simulation.


A user MUST be able to request behaviour in natural language such as turning on Do Not Disturb when Study activates or adding a Planner sidebar surface. AI-generated graph changes MUST be presented as valid graph mutations and the assistant SHOULD explain the resulting behaviour in plain language, with relevant nodes highlightable from the explanation.


If a request would modify protected built-in behaviour, the editor/AI MUST reject that mutation and direct the user toward a user-created Space/full graph instead of attempting an unsafe override.

In a user Space, create a typed graph, save Draft, Validate and Activate; submit natural-language graph changes through the contextual AI bar.

AI changes are real typed mutations with understandable explanation; incompatible hooks show needs-attention rather than destroying the Space.

UI interaction/AI explanation linked to actual nodes and typed action logs.

requirements.requirement: Register Plugin/sidebar contributions per Space using one lifecycle registry and safe rendered surfaces.

sources.quote:
Plugins MUST support contributing custom sidebar elements. An element MUST be able to open an arbitrary configured page/URL, an authorised app surface, an authored CUI page or a generative page, or invoke an Automation or another declared authorised action. Navigation and action-triggering behaviour MUST be explicit. Arbitrary pages remain subject to the existing safe rendering, origin, permissions and external-navigation rules; this capability does not authorise unrestricted code execution.
For each Plugin, the user MUST be able to select which Spaces display its sidebar elements. This selection MUST be inspectable, editable and persisted using stable Plugin, Space and SidebarItem identities. An excluded Space MUST NOT display that Plugin's sidebar contributions merely because the Plugin is installed globally. Sidebar visibility is distinct from permission to execute the Plugin or access Space data; it MUST NOT silently change either.
Attaching a Plugin MUST now be the primary method of supplying custom sidebar elements in custom Spaces. Ordinary Plugin-provided sidebar elements MUST NOT require users to construct a built-in Automation or Space lifecycle graph solely to load the element.
The existing built-in automation/Events & Extensions/full Space graph mechanisms for loading, showing and controlling custom sidebar elements MUST remain supported for enhanced and combined workflows. Plugin and graph routes MUST share the existing sidebar identity, ownership, lifecycle and rendering contracts, preserving AppSurface, CUI and GenerativeUI support. They MUST NOT duplicate the same contribution or replace protected first-party sidebar items. Disabling or detaching a Plugin MUST stop its active contributions without leaving executable orphan actions or deleting unrelated Space content.

Plugin-contributed sidebar elements MUST support this ordinary navigation-row presentation: an icon on the left, a readable text label beside it, and alignment, spacing and interaction treatment consistent with neighbouring sidebar items. A custom entry can sit directly beneath New Chat within the selected Space's permitted custom-sidebar area; it MUST NOT require opening a separate Plugin panel simply to reach the entry.
The screenshot is a concept reference for the custom entry's presentation and placement, not a requirement to copy its project names, conversation history, colours or complete sidebar structure. Existing protected navigation and Space-scoping requirements remain in force. The Plugin's per-Space visibility selection still determines where its entries appear, and the existing automation/Space-graph route remains supported.
Plugin sidebar API and acceptance
Extend the canonical Plugin and Spaces APIs for contribution registration, configuration, removal, per-Space visibility and authorised action dispatch; UI and API MUST use the same stable SidebarItemID and ownership/lifecycle rules. Test Plugin-defined URL/page, authored CUI, generative-page and Automation actions; persistence after restart; visibility only in selected Spaces; keyboard navigation and accessible names; and safe disable/detach without orphan actions or deletion of unrelated content. The original automation/Events & Extensions/Space-graph contribution route MUST continue to work, including combined workflows without duplicate contributions. The Plugin manifest and Builder MUST expose these contribution contracts rather than creating a second sidebar registry.

Space extension graphs MAY add custom sidebar items without replacing protected built-in items. Every custom SidebarItem MUST have stable SidebarItemID, title, icon, order/placement, visibility condition where supported, InterfaceType, interface reference/definition and required permissions.


Supported InterfaceType families MUST include AppSurface, CUI and GenerativeUI. AppSurface embeds an authorised surface from another 9to1 app such as Planner, Files, Boards, Maps, Stack or another declared embeddable surface while preserving canonical owning-app behaviour. CUI renders an explicitly authored safe interface backed by typed state/actions. GenerativeUI renders a Dulche-generated interface constrained by the Generative UI schema/component/action rules.


Generative sidebar interfaces MAY be Dynamic (regenerated/refreshed from current authorised context) or Persisted (stored definition until explicitly regenerated/edited). Generated UI MUST NOT execute arbitrary code or gain permissions merely because it is displayed.


Protected built-in sidebar IDs/namespaces cannot be shadowed/overwritten by extensions. Custom entries use extension-owned stable IDs.

A Task may invoke persistent Agents, Dulche Subagents and tools, and may itself be launched by an Automation, but Task identity remains the user-level work item rather than becoming an Agent or Automation.

Both use the same task identity, persistence, steering, dashboard, verification, permission and resource-control contracts. Preserve the distinction between a configured Assistant/Specialist and the workers delegated to execute a task; delegating work does not create another personal assistant or permission grant.

sources.quote:
1. Outcome-centred persistence
Use persistence by default for substantial agentic requests: “build X” continues until the agreed X is delivered and verified, subject to user-defined scope, checkpoints and stop instructions. Small one-off requests remain single tasks unless persistence is requested.
Retain the objective, constraints, acceptance criteria, plan, valid outputs and remaining work across turns and supported interruptions. A turn limit, completed subtask or initial artifact is not overall completion. Continue towards the agreed outcome, not an expanding backlog of invented features or endless optional polishing.

7. Verification-first completion
Verification is a default, first-class part of execution, not a separate request or optional final message. Before declaring work finished, visually inspect its rendered interface/output and test real intended workflows using the actual artifact or build. Non-visual work requires appropriate direct checks; a build passing or code looking plausible is not proof of the requested behaviour.
If a test fails, diagnose, repair and rerun affected checks and relevant regression tests autonomously until all pass. Continue within the agreed scope, permissions and resource limits. Unavailable verification remains visibly outstanding and may cause NEEDS INPUT or BLOCKED; never fabricate evidence, silently waive tests or claim success.
Record the current artifact/build revision, test result and supporting observation, screenshot or tool output. Invalidate affected results after changes. COMPLETED is an intermediate green-tick state; the default finished handoff is VERIFIED, with a gold tick, delivered artifacts and inspectable evidence. A user-directed stop may leave unverified work but must not be described as verified.

Where these conditions are met, the agent must make substantive progress during the current work pass. Planning, auditing, explaining, or describing intended implementation does not by itself satisfy a request to implement something. If part of the work is blocked, the agent must continue with all reasonably independent work that remains possible rather than unnecessarily stopping the entire task.

All work performed by the agent must result in something genuinely useful for its stated purpose. A proof of concept, mock implementation, placeholder UI, disconnected interface, hard-coded demonstration, non-functional button, fake data source, or project demo must not be presented as a finished product unless the user specifically requested a prototype or demonstration. Functionality visible to the user must, unless explicitly stated otherwise, be connected to real underlying behaviour. Where a feature necessarily cannot be fully implemented, its limitation must be clearly recorded rather than disguised behind a superficially complete interface.

User-added acceptance tests
Users can add tests to the task or an individual checkpoint from the dashboard at any time. Each test records a short requirement, an observable pass condition, its result, current evidence and the result revision. Show PASS, FAIL, NOT RUN, RUNNING, BLOCKED or STALE as appropriate; only PASS satisfies a test.

Default acceptance criteria
All seven criteria below must be true; retain these compact forms in agent context.
Objective
Usability — Can an intended non-technical user understand and use any interface without developer guidance?
Product fit — Does the result look, feel and behave like a complete product of its intended type, with the expected capabilities and workflows, preserving existing functionality in forks or redesigns unless the user explicitly authorises its removal?
Functionality — Is all functionality stated in the request, specification or agreed scope included, fully implemented and usable through its intended workflows, working reliably and consistently end-to-end without omissions, stubs or simulated success?
Integration — Is each feature discoverable and grouped by purpose in the relevant menu, toolbar, panel or screen, with consistent controls and shared project state, rather than crowded into one screen or isolated from normal workflows?
Separation and authenticity — Is user-facing content free of unintended developer notes, test content and unfinished placeholders, with working actions and genuine state instead of promises of unimplemented behaviour, simulated success or sample data presented as real?
Subjective
User fit — Does the result meet the user's stated needs and constraints?
Refinement — Have worthwhile in-scope improvements been applied without sacrificing quality, speed or features?
For interface-free work, record why an interface-dependent condition is satisfied without claiming that visual testing occurred; never use this to omit a required interface. Support subjective judgements with a short evidence-based rationale, not invented user feedback. Refinement concerns identified, material improvements within scope, not proof that no imaginable improvement exists.
Product fit: a LibreOffice Writer UI rewrite must retain Writer's existing capabilities and expose them through the new interface unless the user approves specific removals. A Save/Bold-only shell fails even when the engine remains underneath. A word processor must support document-editing workflows, not require website/component-block construction, backend editing or read-only PDF interaction. Simplifying the interface does not authorise simplifying away the product.
Functionality: verify coverage against the full request, specification and retained feature baseline, not just the implemented subset. Exercise the real user workflows and their effects, including persistence where required. Hidden APIs, static demonstrations or deleting unchecked requirements do not satisfy required user-facing features. Any functionality presented as available must actually work; removing its label does not waive an agreed requirement.
Integration: group text formatting together, place page controls in page layout and account controls in settings, unless an alternative is requested. Controls must operate on the relevant document/selection and reflect shared state. Scattered tools, unrelated controls crammed onto one screen and disconnected demonstrations fail.
Separation and authenticity: Save must actually persist work; a promise to implement saving does not count. A users list must use its intended data source or show an honest empty/loading/error state, not pretend hard-coded Bob/Alice entries are real. Future-tense help text is acceptable when the action works. Explicitly approved prototypes or labelled sample data may serve their requested purpose, but cannot prove live functionality. Deliberate developer tools and the task dashboard may show relevant technical information; accidental implementation notes must not leak into the delivered user-facing product.

requirements.requirement: Plan, probe, batch, verify and recover tool work efficiently through supported contracts.

sources.quote:
8. Tool-call optimisation and batching
Optimise time and cost to a verified result, not tool-call volume. Apply to all agents, including ordinary chat models performing agentic work, Assistants, Specialists and delegated workers. Default to: probe when uncertain → plan the whole work unit → batch execute → verify → repair. Do not insert fresh model reasoning between predictable individual operations.


Probe only when needed — Read the relevant tool contract and reuse verified knowledge for the same tool/version/environment. If behaviour is unfamiliar or uncertain, run a minimal, reversible representative test: one object, or the smallest batch needed to check bulk behaviour. Inspect actual units, axes, placement, scale, rotation, asset references and returned IDs as applicable. Delete only the test objects using their recorded IDs and confirm cleanup before production work. Prefer safe staging or dry-run support where available. Repeat probes only when relevant assumptions change; a successful small probe does not establish large-batch capacity.


Plan the whole work unit — Design the complete building, track or other coherent deliverable before executing its repetitive operations. Prepare a deterministic operation manifest containing the assets, transforms/parameters, dependencies, expected outputs and checks; validate it before submission. Generate repetitive data programmatically where supported instead of individually reasoning through each item. Revise the plan when new evidence, failures or user steering require it, not after every successful operation.


Batch execution — Submit the complete validated work unit in one supported bulk call when safe. Otherwise use bounded chunks, or a supported authorised script/executor that runs the planned calls without a model turn per item. Do not invent a bulk endpoint or assume every MCP supports batching. Where no suitable executor exists, use the available calls efficiently and disclose the constraint rather than claiming a batch occurred. Preserve dependency ordering; parallelise only independent operations that the service can safely process.


Adaptive limits — Choose batch size from known or measured payload, timeout, rate, memory, recovery and responsiveness limits. Start conservatively when capacity is unknown, increase after successful observations and reduce or change approach after failures. Do not jump from one successful test object to 50,000 untested placements. Keep execution interruptible at supported safe boundaries so steering, pause and cancellation remain effective. Batching never expands permissions or bypasses per-action approval requirements.


Verify and recover — Check results after each logical batch or bounded chunk using actual state readback and appropriate visual inspection; verify the assembled result against the manifest and acceptance criteria. For a map, inspect the actual scene from useful views and test relevant traversal/collision behaviour, not merely the reported object count. A successful tool response or sampled visual check alone does not verify the whole deliverable. Repair affected items and rerun relevant checks. Track per-item outcomes and created IDs; after partial failure or timeout, reconcile actual state before retrying, preserve successful work and avoid duplicates. Roll back only identified task-owned changes where safe, never unrelated user work.


Avoid redundant overhead — Reuse current schemas, asset lookups and unchanged results; refresh when invalidated or freshness matters. Batch related reads, request only needed fields and keep large manifests/logs outside repeated model context, with concise summaries and retrievable evidence. Avoid per-object screenshots, explanations, schema rediscovery and busy polling when batch-level evidence suffices. Record real batch/checkpoint progress in the existing dashboard without turning every object into a checkpoint. Efficiency must never weaken quality, required checks or the final verification gate.

Tool-efficiency release checks: demonstrate unfamiliar-tool probing and cleanup, reuse of valid tool knowledge, whole-unit planning, supported batching/chunking without per-object replanning, visual and functional verification, partial-failure recovery without duplicates, and steering at safe boundaries. Compare elapsed time, model turns and tool round trips with a per-item baseline on the same representative task and acceptance tests; efficiency gains must preserve output quality and verification coverage.

sources.quote:
Spaces MUST support explicit memory/context scopes including conversation-local, Space-level and permitted broader personal/team/organisation scopes. Space-level persistent memory/context lives through Dulche Den under stable Space identity and applicable permissions.


Shared Spaces MUST NOT implicitly expose a participant’s private personal Den context or private connected accounts. Caller-specific private context remains private unless deliberately shared through an authorised shared/team mechanism.

Memory can be scoped so unrelated Agents/apps do not receive unnecessary context. Supported scopes should include global/user memory plus narrower project, Agent, app/surface or other explicit contexts where appropriate. Retrieval MUST respect both scope and permission.
Creation and retrieval
Dulche may create or update memories from eligible conversations/context according to the user's Memory Frequency and memory policy. Retrieval is relevance-based: only memories useful to the active request/context should be injected, rather than the complete memory store.
Explicit user corrections supersede contradictory earlier memories. Den MUST retain enough provenance/revision information to distinguish an explicit user statement from an inference and to avoid repeatedly resurfacing a memory that has been corrected, superseded or deleted.
Memory Frequency
Settings MUST expose a Memory Frequency preference with exactly four user-facing levels: Never, Sometimes, Often and Always. The selected level controls how readily Dulche autonomously creates, reinforces or updates Persistent Memory from eligible non-temporary interactions.
* Never: Dulche MUST NOT autonomously create, reinforce or update Persistent Memory from ordinary interactions. Direct user-invoked memory-management actions are separate explicit operations.
* Sometimes: use a conservative threshold and retain only clearly durable, repeatedly useful or high-value information.
* Often: use a lower threshold and remember useful preferences, decisions, entities and ongoing context more readily when they are likely to help future responses.
* Always: evaluate every eligible interaction for durable memory and normally retain information that satisfies the memory policy, while still deduplicating noise, respecting scope/retention rules and avoiding ineligible information.
Changing Memory Frequency affects future autonomous memory behaviour; it MUST NOT silently delete existing memories. The setting is independent of Background Learning.
Temporary chats in Spaces
Spaces can provide Temporary Chats. Persistent Memory creation is disabled inside a Temporary Chat regardless of the user's Memory Frequency. While a chat is temporary, Dulche MUST NOT autonomously create, update, reinforce, merge or promote Persistent Memory from that conversation.
Any explicit action that would save new Persistent Memory from a Temporary Chat must be unavailable or clearly report that memory creation is disabled for temporary chats. Temporary-chat memory-write suppression MUST NOT be bypassed by an Agent, plugin, Skill, tool or Background Learning pipeline.
This rule governs memory creation/writes. Whether existing authorised memories are retrieved into a temporary chat is a separate context/privacy policy and MUST NOT be inferred from the memory-write prohibition.
Management and lifecycle
Users must be able to inspect, search, edit/correct, supersede and delete persistent memories through the appropriate settings/Den surfaces. Deletion and retention use Den's normal lifecycle, sync and purge contracts. Memory export/import must preserve scopes, provenance and deletion/supersession semantics rather than flattening entries into plain prose.

* Shortcut and focus-state presentation.
Focus order follows semantic/tree/layout order unless explicitly overridden. Inactive elements cannot receive user focus. Hidden-but-interactive controls are technically representable under CUI's Hidden semantics, but first-party accessibility lint MUST reject invisible focusable/interactive constructs unless an explicit justified accessibility contract is supplied.
Reduced motion, high contrast, scaling/zoom and non-colour-only state communication MUST be framework-level capabilities rather than app-specific reinventions.
Localisation and directionality
CUI MUST support resource-backed/localisable user-visible strings, locale-aware number/date formatting and right-to-left directionality. Direction/layout mirroring is framework-managed where applicable. Literal developer/debug strings MAY remain literal; shipping product copy SHOULD use the localisation/resource system.

CUI MUST expose a semantic test/accessibility tree so automated tests can locate elements by ID, role, accessible name and other stable semantic selectors rather than raw screen coordinates when semantic targeting exists.
The test harness MUST be able to render a CUI Page/Prefab at declared dimensions, Theme, scale, accessibility/reduced-motion settings and platform capability profile; interact through semantic input; inspect resulting state; and capture deterministic visual evidence where applicable.
Performance and rendering
CUI MUST use Avalonia's mature low-level rendering/composition foundations while adding CUI-level invalidation, dependency and component semantics without introducing unnecessary full-tree work.
* Live variable changes invalidate only dependent expressions/properties/subtrees.
* Virtualisable lists/grids/trees MUST use framework virtualisation rather than constructing every off-screen item by default.
* Backdrop Blur/Refract/Gradient processing MAY use compositor caching, but cache invalidation MUST remain live and correct when sampled content changes.
* Animation/input loops MUST avoid blocking application/domain work on the UI thread.
* Caches must be bounded and revision/dependency invalidated.
Performance acceptance requires measured evidence on the declared supported-hardware/platform baseline. 'Looks fast' is not sufficient.
Platform and Home runtime integration
Native CUI applications depend on the compatible Home-managed CUI/shared runtime under the global Home runtime-dependency contract. The CUI compiler/toolchain belongs to the development/build environment; the runtime version/capability requirement is recorded in app/package metadata.
Web CUI MAY use a browser-specific implementation/runtime, but it MUST preserve the same public CUI semantics, component contracts, state identities and supported action/property behaviour except for explicitly declared platform capability differences.
Platform differences such as unsupported backdrop effects, specialised renderer capabilities or input hardware MUST be capability-negotiated explicitly. The runtime MUST NOT silently reinterpret unsupported CUI into materially different behaviour.

Cakemods.com MUST host a web version of every 9-1 Workspace/AI product that is not explicitly listed as web-exempt. Web surfaces MUST share the same CAKE ID identity, canonical artifact formats, domain APIs, permission model and underlying server-side entities as desktop equivalents. Browser-specific UI/layout MAY differ, but it MUST NOT create a separate incompatible product model.




The default rule is to provide a web version whenever the product’s core value can sensibly work in a browser. Browser-specific capability limits are acceptable when they are explicit and the useful core product remains intact; a single desktop-only feature is not by itself a reason to omit an otherwise useful web app.


Web exemption is permitted only when the product’s core function requires infrastructure, privileged device access or hosted compute that CAKE does not currently provide. Each exemption MUST state the blocking capability/infrastructure. Exemptions MUST be re-evaluated when that blocker is removed; exemption is not a permanent product classification.

Desktop and web MUST use the same CAKE ID, account identity, organisation context and entitlement services. Ordinary users MUST NOT require WordPress accounts.
Authentication MUST preserve the existing secure public-client contract, including the specified browser-based authorisation flow or an explicitly equivalent secure implementation. Clients MUST NOT contain provider credentials, billing secrets or entitlement-signing secrets.
The supported registration, sign-in, sign-out, recovery, profile, session-inspection and session-revocation journeys MUST work against the production backend. Any journey that sends verification or recovery email MUST use a configured delivery service and expose delivery failures honestly.
Any transition from WordPress-linked authentication MUST use verified account mappings and recovery rules. Matching a mutable username MUST NOT transfer account ownership, administrative authority or paid entitlements.
Jacob’s reserved @CroakyJake handle and account-bound free Business feature grant MUST survive the transition. That grant MUST NOT become an exemption from resource accounting, security permissions or third-party spending approval.
Browser applications MUST use authenticated equivalents of Home’s shared services without requiring a local Home installation. Permission approval, trust, revocation and audit semantics MUST remain consistent with native applications.
Personal and organisation contexts MUST remain separate throughout navigation, storage, billing, search and AI access. Switching accounts or organisations MUST NOT expose cached private information from the previous context.
SH-06 — Full browser versions of the applications
Every non-exempt Workspace and AI application MUST have a functional browser version.
The target is the same application on the web, not a companion dashboard, viewer-only edition or simplified alternative. At equivalent viewport sizes, the browser version MUST preserve the desktop application’s information architecture, tools, editor structure, commands, menus, selection behaviour, settings and supported workflows.
Browser-specific adaptations are permitted for actual capability differences and responsive layouts. They MUST NOT justify avoidable feature loss.
Web implementations MUST preserve CUI’s public semantics, shared component contracts, canonical state identities and supported actions. A browser-specific runtime is permitted; an independently redesigned, incompatible UI framework is not the intended outcome.
Each app MUST support its applicable create, open, edit, save, reopen, history, import/export, sharing and recovery operations. The shared contextual AI bar MUST operate on the real semantic artifact through authorised owning-app APIs.
The web inventory MUST include the active Terra-form additions: Link, Prototype, Paths, Replay, Files’ organisation types and Variants in their owning applications. These retain their existing ownership and terminology; they MUST NOT be reorganised into different products for the web implementation.
Each application MUST have a capability matrix identifying supported browser operations, equivalent adaptations and exact remaining restrictions. A restriction MUST identify the missing capability, affected operation, user-visible behaviour and validation evidence.
A desktop-only feature is not sufficient reason to omit an otherwise useful web app. Mini Computer retains its existing web exemption unless the required hosted-compute capability is explicitly provided. Other missing native capabilities MUST NOT be represented as available merely because a browser interface exists.
Direct links, browser refresh, back/forward navigation and account restoration MUST preserve the intended application and artifact context. Unsupported browsers MUST receive a meaningful compatibility state rather than a broken interface.

The single trusted installer MUST install Home, all mandatory modules, the selected app and its app-required dependencies. Selecting a second app MUST reuse compatible shared packages. Internal platform package formats may be used; separate user-facing standalone MSIX installers for individual apps are not the distribution model. Native Windows and 9to1-OS use this contract through their supported packaging mechanisms. Browser apps use authenticated shared web services and MUST NOT require a local Home installation.
Before a niche feature needs an absent optional module, show the required component, download/storage impact and Install/Cancel controls. A cancelled or failed install preserves the user's work and intended action; retry is explicit and safe. A required dependency cannot be uninstalled while an installed app depends on it. Uninstalling an optional app preserves user artifacts and dependencies required elsewhere. Updates, repair and rollback use staged validation and atomic activation; interruption MUST preserve or recover the previous valid installation.
Opening an artifact or embedded app whose required app/module is absent MUST offer the same trusted install path, or an explicit unavailable state when installation is unsupported. It MUST NOT silently download unrelated apps, create a substitute viewer with lost capabilities, or claim a module is available solely because another Mesh device has it.
Acceptance: clean-install one chosen app without unrelated optional apps; add another without duplicated core; decline and retry a feature-module install; reject removal of an in-use dependency; interrupt an update and recover; uninstall/reinstall without losing artifacts; verify Home version negotiation and the browser/no-local-Home case.

Deliver release artifacts and a manifest identifying product/platform, version, exact commit, cryptographic hash, launch/install instructions and known limitations. Re-run clean install, upgrade, dependency failure, repair and rollback against those exact artifacts. Implementation, verification, deployment and public release approval remain distinct states.
Lunar Eclipse is complete only when every in-scope behaviour is integrated and verified, required inherited suites pass, artifacts install/run cleanly, and no unresolved mandatory failure is concealed. A remaining genuine external gate or approved scoped exception must identify the affected requirement/platform, impact and evidence; it does not count as verified functionality. A worker may not mark the pass complete merely because its allocated task list ended.
LE-15 — Explicit external decisions
Existing Sol Happy commercial/production decisions remain authoritative: undefined subscription lifecycle, retention/grace policy, live service configuration, approved resource budgets and production cutover/spending require their existing approvals. Do not invent them in this pass. Implement enforceable local behaviour, tested entitlement hooks and non-destructive failure states while affected live paths remain visibly blocked. This section adds no new fee, provider, donor or release deadline.
